### Composition-change event contract

- The intended class name is `GuiGraphicsComposition`, in `Source/Application/GraphicsCompositions/GuiGraphicsComposition.cpp`. Declare `CompositionUpdateType` and the new event-argument type immediately above `GuiWindow` in `Source/Application/Controls/GuiWindowControls.h`. Follow the existing `GuiEventArgs` / `Description<T>` convention and expose `ChildCompositionUpdated` as a typed graphics event, associated with the window's bounds composition.
- `parent` is the composition whose child collection changed; `child` is the directly inserted, removed, or reordered child. The event belongs to that composition's owning `GuiWindow`, including a logical hosted window. It is a notification, not a cancelable request, and its pointers do not transfer ownership.
- Notify once after a successful structural change and its existing parent/control/host bookkeeping have completed. Failed insert/remove/move calls, detached-tree mutations, and `MoveChild` to the existing index produce no event. `AddChild` already delegates to `InsertChild`, so it must not add a second notification.
- Capture the owning window before removal disconnects the subtree. A removal notification exposes the old parent and live removed child while the parent's collection already excludes that child. Insertion and move notifications expose the resulting collection order. Resolve the owner from the parent/host context, not from the removed child's now-cleared control ancestry.
- Reparenting is the existing remove followed by insert, with one notification to each affected window. Attaching a populated subtree produces one notification; the UIA listener scans that subtree internally to discover its semantic descendants. Such scanning does not recursively raise `ChildCompositionUpdated`.
- Event arguments are valid for synchronous notification only. Deferred UIA work must retain provider/lifetime state rather than raw composition pointers. Account for reentrant handlers and construction/destruction: do not deliver through an incompletely constructed or already destructed `GuiWindow` event, and do not access a removed child after subscribers may have deleted it.
- Register the event, enum, and argument fields using the existing patterns in `Source/Reflection/TypeDescriptors/GuiReflectionPlugin.h`, `GuiReflectionControls.cpp`, and `GuiReflectionEvents.cpp`. This is a cross-platform public event even though the provider consuming it is Windows-only. Regenerate both architectures' metadata as required by `Project.md`.

### Windows listener, threading, and lifetime

- The four named public setup functions delegate to `SetupWindowsGDIRendererInternal` in `Source/PlatformProviders/Windows/GDI/WinGDIApplication.cpp` and `SetupWindowsDirect2DRendererInternal` in `Source/PlatformProviders/Windows/Direct2D/WinDirect2DApplication.cpp`. Those shared implementations own the existing `listener` variables: rename them to `nativeListener` there and wire `uiaListener` for both ordinary and hosted routes without duplicating setup. Raw renderer routes also pass through these functions; they must not expose a fabricated semantic GacUI tree when no local `GuiApplication` owns it.
- `IWindowsForm::InstallMessageHandler` retains a `Ptr<INativeMessageHandler>`, whereas controller callback registration uses a raw listener pointer. Give `uiaListener` one owning `Ptr` and pass that ownership through message-handler installation; do not imitate the existing native listener's stack allocation or create a second owning `Ptr` from `.Obj()`.
- If teardown uses `UninstallMessageHandler`, fix its existing removal bug in `Source/PlatformProviders/Windows/WinNativeWindow.cpp`: it computes `index` but passes `handler` to `messageHandlers.RemoveAt`, which must receive `index`. Treat this as a narrow prerequisite to using the existing handler API, and verify removal with multiple installed handlers.
- In hosted mode, observe both actual native-window lifecycle and hosted logical-window lifecycle. The real controller owns the HWND; the hosted controller reports virtual subwindows. Resolve all hosted providers to the one actual HWND, attach logical windows beneath the main root, and preserve their own descendants and semantics. Ordinary windows retain their separate HWND roots. Do not treat a virtual `INativeWindow` as an `IWindowsForm`.
- `GuiWindow` creates its native window before `SetNativeWindow` and `GuiApplication::RegisterWindow` finish. Install the message hook when notified, but defer semantic binding until construction has completed, checking that the recorded window is still alive. Seed existing windows and attached subtrees before exposing their providers. Retain associations for teardown because native destruction occurs after the application has unregistered the `GuiWindow`.
- Handle `WM_GETOBJECT` for `UiaRootObjectId` through `INativeMessageHandler::AfterHandle`, setting the result and `skip` so the default procedure does not overwrite it; `BeforeHandle` cannot supply that result. Compare the object identifier using the documented signed convention. Return `UiaReturnRawElementProvider` only for a live, initialized root, and leave other object IDs to their existing handling. Use `UiaHostProviderFromHwnd` for the actual HWND root's host provider, not every semantic child. See [WM_GETOBJECT handling](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/winauto/handling-the-wm-getobject-message).
- GacUI objects are UI-thread-only, but these Windows setup functions initialize COM as MTA. `ProviderOptions_UseComThreading` alone therefore does not marshal calls to the GacUI thread. Dispatch reads and writes through a defined UI-thread boundary, execute directly when already on that thread, and avoid holding locks while waiting or raising UIA events. UiaList and script clients should make calls and manage subscriptions on a windowless MTA worker, following [UIA client threading](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/winauto/uiauto-threading).
- `IInvokeProvider::Invoke` must queue the action and return without waiting through modal UI. Validate the target's lifetime again when the queued action executes; avoid a blocking UI invocation that deadlocks the inspector while a dialog is open. See [Invoke requirements](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/uiautomationcore/nf-uiautomationcore-iinvokeprovider-invoke).
- Keep hook state separate from exposed-tree membership and COM wrapper lifetime. Reuse existing internal-property/lifetime facilities to own per-object state; hook once, ignore ordinary callbacks while detached, and invalidate destroyed targets even when clients retain wrappers. Seed hooks independently of client enumeration. Reattachment, theme replacement, and list recycling must not duplicate subscriptions or make an old provider refer to a different object at a reused address.
- Return UIA's documented unavailable/unsupported/disabled results for those expected states; do not dereference stale controls or advertise a pattern whose operations are only stubs. Retire providers during teardown without returning them again to reentrant `WM_GETOBJECT` requests. `UiaDisconnectProvider` cannot run inside a synchronous `SendMessage` call; defer that COM cleanup when necessary, after marking the target unavailable. See [provider disconnection](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/uiautomationcoreapi/nf-uiautomationcoreapi-uiadisconnectprovider).

## No.1 [CONFIRMED] Native Windows UIA and inspector integration

Use the existing composition host and internal-property lifetime facilities, model callbacks and control events. New Windows provider code belongs in UIAutomation; shared code only gains the requested reflected composition event and setup wiring. Keep UIA COM calls behind a main-thread dispatcher and asynchronous Invoke. Migrate endpoint arguments with strict validation while keeping protocol traffic on 8888.

### CODE CHANGE

The concurrent verification harness refreshes process discovery after all targets start, identifies each process-owned HWND rather than a duplicate title occurrence, waits for the Nodes/detail views, and selects a node before opening its properties with Enter. The inspector driver's scroll search advances less than a viewport so virtualized rows are not skipped.

Final ordinary shutdown testing exposed a property-refresh performance defect after palette replacement. CDB showed the UI thread in UiaCombo during a root notification, repeatedly searching 2874 recorded nodes for each list-selection property. Maintain a UI-thread-owned index of combo provider nodes and search only those live owners. Preserve the existing lifetime and contained-list validation; do not relax the shutdown deadline.

Header review adds the actual column-model Transform.Resize capability and sorting ItemStatus. Header Move/Rotate remain unsupported. Sorting, shortcut, orientation, content-view and changing pattern availability are included in property notifications. Window Transform operations check their capability flags and use the real hosted HWND for root resizing. The list-view and window tests verify size changes and restore them.

The extended inspector regression found an expected UIA_E_ELEMENTNOTAVAILABLE from SupportedTextSelection on one synthetic text-pattern interface while the element and its other text interfaces remained readable. Isolate expected per-pattern inspection errors in a visible error readout after rechecking the element itself; continue propagating unexpected failures and actually unavailable elements. Keep the error's operation and HRESULT visible instead of replacing it with a generic unsupported caption.

Final semantic review found that GuiMenuButton inherits GuiSelectableButton but disables automatic selection. Dispatch command/submenu/split behavior before generic selectable-button behavior; expose toolbar/ribbon/tooltip/separator roles and multiline Document semantics from the existing class and state. Use menu and tooltip lifecycle events, keep editable contents in Value/Text rather than Name, and report actual shortcut/orientation properties. Add targeted menu/toolbar and multiline assertions before repeating the two complete UIA suites.

Implemented composition/reflection notifications, UI-thread Windows providers and model hooks, semantic item and text-range providers, four renderer routes, inspector getter/action fixes, strict automation argument parsing, project inventories and generated metadata/resources. Runtime verification exposed transposed date-picker dimension accessors (index 42 at row 6) and missing hosted physical-screen offsets; the Windows adapter accounts for both without modifying shared calendar APIs. Verification scripts and final results follow below.

The inspector already had an Invoke catalog entry; do not fabricate Invoke on every element or equate the Legacy bridge with a native Invoke provider. The independent native button displays its Invoke section and each deliberate command increments its counter once. GacUI commands now expose actual Invoke through the new provider. The original reported elements were not identified, so the report does not claim their missing-Invoke symptom or Legacy crash was reproduced. Legacy commands now check default-action text and current state again at execution, and expected stale/unsupported results remain visible errors. Pure getters have explicit classification, committed-parameter queries and generation checks; listening and range-workspace commands remain deliberate actions.

Runtime corrections also preserve combo selection through the owning combo, commit date editor selection through DateSelected, give active grid editors their logical cell parent, and omit the replaced visualizer subtree. Text snapshots map the second UTF-16 unit of CRLF/surrogate pairs to valid carets: CDB traced the prior GetVisibleRanges failure to DirectWrite lineMetrics[-1] when a CRLF continuation was passed as a caret. Semantic rescans are deferred until composition construction/destruction callbacks finish.

Normal HTTP !Exit exposed a tree-root lifetime bug. CDB found WindowsUIAutomationLifetime detaching its tree callback through a freed vtable; items and columns were already null. NodeRootProviderBase does not notify destruction through OnAttached(nullptr), so the hook now owns that root until it detaches on the UI thread. Retired logical nodes release model references on that thread. GetRuntimeId uses immutable provider identity during UiaDisconnectProvider, without querying the already retired control. Scroll/range/view properties are included in change notifications.

Concurrent launches exposed an existing FullControlTest global-hotkey collision: the second process legitimately receives no shortcut, but the label binding dereferenced it. CDB traced this to the generated binding's GetShortcut()->GetName. The authored resource now supplies a fallback label; both architecture outputs are regenerated with GacUI_Compiler.

Full traversal identified a visibility distinction: GuiControl.Visible does not mean that an HWND or hosted window is open. Use GuiControlHost.GetOpening for semantic window membership and bounds, seed hooks on hidden registered windows, and publish WindowOpened/WindowClosed plus hosted-parent structure notifications. Provider actions also respect native window disabled state while modal UI is open.

CDB traced the gender-popup failure to Parent treating the combo display's GuiListItemTemplate as a logical list row. Such display templates have no associated list owner. Only map templates to logical rows/cells when they are associated with a list; otherwise continue normal composition ancestry. This preserves the display control's actual parent without constructing a provider for a null control.

The full text scenario exposed paint-dependent embedded-object enumeration. GuiDocumentCommonInterface hides item containers until OnRenderEmbeddedObject marks them visible. Enumerate document children from the current DocumentModel placeholders and registered document items, respecting child-local visibility without inheriting the renderer-controlled container visibility. Use this same mapping for fragment children and TextRange.GetChildren, so offscreen or not-yet-painted objects remain semantic document children.

Hosted Transform.Move now moves the actual HWND for the main root and subtracts the actual host's client-screen origin for logical subwindows. GuiHostedWindowProxy_Main intentionally clamps its own logical position to zero, so moving that virtual window could never implement the root's screen-coordinate contract. The window scenario checks relative native-HWND movement and hosted subwindow screen bounds. Popup checks wait for native popup exposure before selecting their contents.

The ordinary-popup timeout was a harness discovery error: Windows UIA placed an owned popup HWND beneath its owner in the desktop tree, rather than among desktop children. A live MTA inspection found the popup list and its correct combo SelectionContainer under that owner. Ordinary-window discovery now enumerates the launched process's visible native HWNDs and queries each root with FromHandle, covering both desktop placements and operating-system dialogs such as #32770.

Ordinary message dialogs use Windows' native button proxy. Its Invoke failed in MS.Internal.AutomationProxies.Misc.SendInput while focusing the button on the locked desktop. The GacUI Invoke that opened the modal returned promptly and the native dialog's Window pattern was readable. The harness logs this specific proxy failure and dismisses the verified owned native Button HWND with BM_CLICK; it does not suppress failures from GacUI providers. This native proxy path remains a locked-session verification limitation.

### CONFIRMED

All commands below use absolute script paths under `C:\Code\VczhLibraries\GacUI`. Build and application wrappers run from the documented solution directory. UI interaction suites run sequentially, with windowless MTA clients and process-owned HWND discovery.

- `copilotBuild.ps1 -Configuration Debug -Platform Win32` and `-Platform x64`, from `Test/GacUISrc`: zero warnings/errors. Repeated after final provider corrections.
- `copilotExecute.ps1 -Mode UnitTest -Executable UnitTest -Configuration Debug -Platform Win32` and `-Platform x64`: 90/90 files, 1769/1769 cases, no appended Debug leak report. The new composition case verifies detached/attached operations, rejection/no-op behavior, exact parent/child and final state, reparenting, populated subtree notification, reflection subscription and teardown. A final additional Win32 run again passed all 1769 cases with no appended leak report. Six existing snapshot files differed only in the working-directory path/derived width and transient focus colors; those environmental changes were inspected and restored.
- `Metadata_Generate` and `Metadata_Test`, through `copilotExecute.ps1 -Mode CLI`, completed for both architectures. The documented sequence was repeated after `GacUI_Compiler` completed all nine resource groups and both architectures. Generated outputs were not hand-edited.
- `Tools/UiaList/Verification/CheckCatalog.ps1`: 175 properties, 35 patterns, 44 text attributes, 41 control types, one metadata ID and 43 synchronized translation keys; inventories/locales passed.
- UiaList Debug Win32/x64 and Release Win32/x64 final builds all completed with zero warnings/errors. Fixture Debug Win32/x64 builds completed.
- `Tools/UiaList/Verification/Smoke.ps1 -Platform x64 -FixtureProcessId 26340 -GetterRegression` and `-Platform Win32`: complete workflows passed in 112.46 and 119.79 seconds respectively, both with exit zero. Verified independent exactly-once native Invoke, direct readouts without duplicate buttons, invalid draft rejection, exactly-once committed query, rapid query replacement, returned-element inspection, close/reopen target changes, exactly-once StartListening/Cancel and text-range Clone, and no accidental Invoke.
- The original Legacy target was unspecified, so that original crash is not claimed reproduced or retested. A real Windows MSAA bridge probe logged native target 101 (button: defaultAction `Press`, state `0x00100000`) and target 108 (static label: empty defaultAction, state `0x00000040`). Both direct `DoDefaultAction` calls returned `S_OK`; the inspector correctly withholds its command for an empty default action.
- `Test/AutomationPorts.ps1 -Suite Invalid`: all 45 malformed/empty/duplicate/out-of-range argument cases across nine consumers passed. `-Suite Local`: all six local consumers passed with default 8888 and explicit 8901, normal exit and released endpoints; this includes ordinary full-reflection `CppTest_Reflection` startup.
- `Test/AutomationPorts.ps1 -Suite Remote`: passed five Core/renderer cases, eight CppTest_Rvm host cases across Pipe/Http/MiniHttp/Cli and default/custom ports, and MiniHttp RVMT with a stdio host and split automation endpoint. Protocol listeners remained on 8888. Renderer default 8888 was tested with Pipe; paired examples explicitly used 8889. The existing RVM host intentionally exits 1 on requester disconnect; the harness checks that documented behavior and released listeners.
- `Test/AutomationPorts.ps1 -Suite Release`: final Release UiaList build exposed no endpoint and exited normally with zero.
- `Test/AutomationPorts.ps1 -Suite Concurrent`: two consecutive cycles passed with hosted CppTest on 8888, ordinary CppTest_Metaonly on 8890 and Debug UiaListApp on 8891. UiaList inspected each process-owned root and its Window action section; each target passed 14 independent UIA selection assertions per cycle. All three endpoints remained responsive, then all processes exited normally and endpoints were released before immediate restart.
- Additional GDI smoke: temporary, subsequently restored entrypoints selected GDI in hosted CppTest and ordinary CppTest_Metaonly. Each Window scenario passed 53 assertions and normal shutdown. Both startups also ran nine native message-handler assertions: two handlers each receive Before/After; remove the second handler first; the first still receives messages; repeated removal returns false; removing the first stops both callbacks. Direct2D entrypoints were restored byte-for-byte and rebuilt.
- `Test/UIA_CppTest.ps1`: final full hosted Direct2D run passed 4433 assertions (430 structure, 339 property and 15 text events), normal Window.Close, exit zero and released endpoint.
- `Test/CppTest_Metaonly.ps1`: final full ordinary Direct2D run passed 4445 assertions (415 structure, 324 property and 13 text events), normal Window.Close, exit zero and released endpoint. This also confirms that the combo-owner index fixed the palette-refresh shutdown timeout without increasing the deadline. The focused Window scenarios passed 104 assertions for each mode, including seeded rich-text menu selection and toolbar formatting, physical root resize/move, focus, modal Invoke and subwindow lifecycle.

Verification limitations: Windows' native message-box Invoke proxy requires SendInput for focus and failed on the locked desktop. The harness reports that exact failure, then dismisses only the verified owned native Button with BM_CLICK. GacUI modal Invoke and provider actions remain asserted normally. Physical-screen relative Move checks passed for native roots and hosted subwindows; mixed-DPI monitors, negative desktop origins and manual visual hit-testing/focus have not been verified here. A synthetic TextEdit pattern's SupportedTextSelection returned `0x80040201` while other text interfaces remained usable; this is displayed as a pattern-query error, not reported as successful support.
